newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close higher on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close higher on speculative buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 1.02 percent higher on Monday as locals bought stocks for speculative reasons ahead of the release of fourth quarter earnings results of finance firms from Tuesday, brokers said.
The SET index rose for the second consecutive trading day, advancing 8.48 points to 841.03 on 2.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 0.70 point to 62.87.

"Nobody knows whether how good or bad the fourth quarter earnings results of finance firms that would be released tomorrow would be. Locals bought just for speculative reasons," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.
Advancers led decliners 156 to 118, excluding foreign shares, while 84 issues were unchanged.
Finance companies have agreed to release fourth quarter earnings results tomorrow and some banks may also release their results, brokers said.
"The index moved in narrow range throughout the session today as investors were a bit jittery that earnings results for finance companies would be poorer than earlier expectated," said Thanadech.
Brokers said foreign investors were also not active as they also awaited the earnings results.
The commerce sector gained most, rising 2.56 percent. The banking sector advanced 1.24 percent and the finance sector slipped 0.19 percent.

Bank of Ayudhya topped the active list, rising two baht to 78. Nakornthon Bank slipped 0.50 to 70 after announcing earlier today that its unaudited net profit for 1996 rose to 701.57 million baht against 610.79 million in 1995.
Large capitalised TelecomAsia rose 0.50 to 52.50 and Finance One declined 1.75 to 45.
Support is seen by some brokers at 830 and resistance at 850 on Tuesday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
